title: Pack sizes and expiry information in shared-ingredient cafe replenishment
question: How does a simple expiry-adjusted order-up-to rule compare with equally calibrated pooled base-stock replenishment when pack size, shelf life and shared daily demand-factor variability vary?
forecast: True conditional weekday mean and variance; no realized future demand is supplied to a policy.
calibration: Select z separately for each scenario and policy by mean validation cost. Break ties by lower z. Evaluation paths are disjoint.
inference: Paired differences across 200 independent evaluation replications. Pointwise two-sided 95% Student-t intervals. No population-of-stores inference and no simultaneous 54-cell claim.
objective: Order commitments + unmet ingredient quantity penalty + closing inventory holding cost. Acquisition cost of expired stock is already included in order commitments. Outstanding end-of-horizon orders are included and reported separately.
sensitivity: Use preselected small/large packs, shortest/longest shelf life and largest demand factor CV; repeat for 1095 measurement days with 180 burn-in days using new seeds.
claims: Controlled simulation comparison; no field outcome, optimal-policy claim or first-in-literature claim. Shortage and fill rate refer to ingredient volume.
